from typing import Self

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractBaseUser, AnonymousUser
from django.db import models
from django.utils.text import slugify
from taggit.managers import TaggableManager


class ArticleQuerySet(models.QuerySet):
    def with_favorites(self, user: AbstractBaseUser | AnonymousUser) -> Self:
        return self.annotate(
            num_favorites=models.Count("favorites"),
            is_favorite=(
                models.Exists(get_user_model().objects.filter(pk=user.pk, favorites=models.OuterRef("pk")))
                if user.is_authenticated
                else models.Value(False, output_field=models.BooleanField())
            ),
        )


ArticleManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(ArticleQuerySet)


class Article(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True, blank=False)
    summary = models.TextField(blank=True)
    content = models.TextField(blank=True)

    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    tags = TaggableManager(blank=True)
    favorites = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="favorites")
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True, max_length=255)  # Not a property as used for lookup

    objects = ArticleManager()

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        if not self.pk:
            self.slug = slugify(self.title)
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

content.content:
===authoring.feature===
Feature: Authoring and favoriting articles
  As an author
  I want to create, edit, and delete my own articles, and favorite others' work
  So that I can publish my writing and signal which articles I value

  Authoring is restricted to the article's own author. Favoriting is open to
  any signed-in reader and toggles on each action. Both demand authentication;
  an anonymous visitor is always sent to sign in first.

  Rule: Only a signed-in user may reach the article editor

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor is redirected away from the new-article editor
      When an anonymous visitor opens the new-article editor
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-002
    Scenario: A signed-in author opens the new-article editor
      Given a signed-in author
      When they open the new-article editor
      Then the article editor is presented

  Rule: Publishing an article records its title, summary, body, tags, and author

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-001
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article titled "New Title" with a summary, a body, and the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article is created with that author
      And its summary and body are recorded as entered
      And it carries the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-002
    Scenario: Tag entries are trimmed and blank entries discarded
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article carries exactly the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-003
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with no tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with an empty tag list
      Then the article is created with no tags

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-004
    Scenario: After publishing, the author lands on the new article
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish a valid article
      Then they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-005
    Scenario: An article cannot be published without a title
      Given a signed-in author
      When they submit the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may edit their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot edit the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to open the edit editor for that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-002
    Scenario: The author's editor is pre-filled with the current article
      Given a signed-in author with an article titled "Edit Me" tagged "python"
      When they open the edit editor for that article
      Then the editor is pre-filled with "Edit Me"
      And the editor is pre-filled with the tag "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-003
    Scenario: An author edits the summary, body, and tags of their article
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with a new summary, a new body, and the tags "rust"
      Then the article's summary and body are updated
      And the article carries exactly the tag "rust"
      And they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-004
    Scenario: A saved edit cannot leave the title empty
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may delete their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot delete the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to delete that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-002
    Scenario: An author deletes their own article
      Given a signed-in author with an article
      When they delete that article
      Then the article no longer exists
      And they are returned to the home feed

  Rule: Favoriting requires sign-in and toggles on each action

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot favorite an article
      When an anonymous visitor tries to favorite an article
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-002
    Scenario: Favoriting then favoriting again removes the favorite
      Given a signed-in reader and an article they have not favorited
      When the reader favorites the article
      Then the article counts the reader among its favorites
      When the reader favorites the article again
      Then the article no longer counts the reader among its favorites

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-003
    Scenario: After a non-HTMX favorite the reader returns to the article
      Given a signed-in reader and an article
      When the reader favorites the article through a full request
      Then they are returned to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-004
    Scenario: An HTMX favorite returns only the favorite control
      Given a signed-in reader and an article
      When the reader favorites the article via HTMX
      Then only the favorite control fragment is returned

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-005
    Scenario: Favoriting a non-existent article is reported as not found
      Given a signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to favorite an article that does not exist
      Then the article is reported as not found

  Rule: A profile page lists a user's own articles or their favorites by tab

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-001
    Scenario: The profile's article tab lists articles written by that user
      Given a user who has written several articles
      When a reader opens that user's profile on the articles tab
      Then the user's own articles are listed newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-002
    Scenario: The profile's favorites tab lists articles that user has favorited
      Given a user who has favorited several articles
      When a reader opens that user's profile on the favorites tab
      Then the articles that user has favorited are listed newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-003
    Scenario: A profile for an unknown user is reported as not found
      When a reader opens a profile for a username that does not exist
      Then the profile is reported as not found
===feeds.feature===
Feature: Browsing article feeds
  As a reader
  I want to browse articles through the global feed, my personalised feed, and tag filters
  So that I can discover the writing that matters to me

  The feed is the home surface for articles. A reader can switch between the
  global feed (every article), their personal "following" feed (articles by
  authors they follow), and a tag-filtered view. All three share one feed
  rendering pipeline: the same composition, the same pagination, and the same
  choice between a full page and an in-place fragment refresh.

  Background:
    Given several published articles exist by various authors

  Rule: The global feed shows every article, newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-001
    Scenario: An anonymous reader sees all articles in the global feed
      Given an article "Post One" and an article "Post Two" exist
      When an anonymous reader opens the home feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the global feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-002
    Scenario: Articles are ordered newest first
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then articles appear in order of most recently created first

  Rule: The following feed shows only articles by authors the reader follows

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-001
    Scenario: A signed-in reader sees only followed authors' articles
      Given a reader who follows the author of "Post One"
      And the author of "Post Two" is not followed by that reader
      When the reader opens their following feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they do not see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the following feed

    # @unverified-intent: anonymous access to the following feed is handled by a
    # server-side redirect to login rather than hiding the tab; documenting the
    # current contract.
    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-002
    Scenario: An anonymous reader requesting the following feed is sent to sign in
      When an anonymous reader requests the following feed
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

  Rule: A tag filter narrows the feed to articles carrying that tag

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-001
    Scenario: Filtering the feed by a tag query
      Given "Post One" is tagged "python"
      And "Post Two" is tagged "django"
      When a reader filters the home feed by the tag "python"
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they do not see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the tag feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-002
    Scenario: Visiting a tag's own page narrows the feed the same way
      Given "Post Two" is tagged "django"
      When a reader opens the page for the tag "django"
      Then they see "Post Two"
      And they do not see "Post One"

  Rule: The sidebar offers the set of all tags, refreshed on a short cycle

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-003
    Scenario: The feed presents the available tags
      Given articles tagged "python" and "django" exist
      When a reader opens the home feed
      Then the available tags are offered alongside the feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-004
    Scenario: Newly used tags become available after an article is saved
      Given the available tags have been listed and cached
      When an author publishes an article carrying a brand-new tag
      Then the new tag becomes available to readers immediately

  Rule: Feeds are paginated ten articles to a page

    @RID-ARTICLES-PAGINATION-001
    Scenario: The feed shows at most ten articles per page
      Given more than ten articles exist
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then at most ten articles are shown on the page

    @RID-ARTICLES-PAGINATION-002
    Scenario Outline: A malformed or out-of-bounds page request falls back to the first page
      When a reader opens the feed with a page request of "<requested>"
      Then the feed responds successfully
      And the reader is shown page 1

      Examples:
        | requested |
        | bogus     |
        | 0         |
        | -5        |
        |           |

  Rule: HTMX fragment requests and full page loads share one feed code path

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FRAGMENT-001
    Scenario: A full page load renders the complete feed page
      When a reader opens the home feed as a full page request
      Then the complete feed page is rendered

===specs/README===
# Behavioral specs (FFFlow L3)

These Gherkin feature files are the **behavioral contract** for the app — what
it does, in present tense, in domain language. They were extracted from the
existing code by FFFlow's `characterize` step, so they describe current
behavior (characterization), not aspirations.

## Layout

One directory per bounded context (matching the Django apps + shared helpers):

```
docs/specs/
  accounts/    authentication, profiles & following, user model
  articles/    feeds, authoring, article model, markdown
  comments/    commenting, comment model
  helpers/     pagination, integrity-error classification, htmx detection
```

Acceptance specs live at a context root; domain/property specs live under
`<context>/domain/`. `*-properties.feature` files hold universal invariants
(tagged `@property-based`) suited to property-based testing with Hypothesis.

## RIDs (requirement IDs)

Every scenario carries a unique `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}` tag. The CONTEXT
segment matches the first directory under `docs/specs/`. These are the anchor
points for traceability: spec → test → code.

131 scenarios, 131 RIDs.

## Gates (both blocking, part of `just check-all`)

- **`just spec-audit`** — `specdrive audit`: every RID is well-formed, unique,
  and its CONTEXT matches its directory.
- **`just spec-verify`** — full spec→test traceability. Runs both test suites,
  emits a JUnit report from each, injects each test's RID(s), merges the
  reports, and runs `specdrive verify` with `strictTraceability` on.
  **131/131 RIDs covered, 0 uncovered.**

## How a test declares the scenario it covers

`specdrive verify` reads RIDs from the JUnit report as
`<property name="rid" value="RID-...">` inside each `<testcase>`. The Django
runner doesn't emit per-test properties, so the mapping lives in
`docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml` (`"<classname>::<test_method>": [RID-...]`) and
`scripts/inject_rids.py` writes the properties into the report. 15 tests are
deliberately unmapped (`@NOSPEC`) — seed/CLI commands and bare GET-render
smoke tests with no behavioral scenario.

## Two test suites

- **Django suite** (`apps/*/tests.py`, `helpers/tests.py`, `manage.py test`) —
  the 124 example/behavioral tests, including `hypothesis.extra.django`
  property tests for DB-backed invariants (slug stability, email-identity,
  self-follow).
- **Property suite** (`specs/property/`, pytest + `pytest-bdd-property`) — binds
  the DB-free `@property-based` pagination scenarios directly to the Gherkin
  feature file; Hypothesis generates 100+ inputs per scenario.

## `@unverified-intent`

Seven scenarios carry a `# @unverified-intent:` comment. These pin behavior
that is *currently* true but may be an unintended quirk (e.g. a self-follow is a
silent no-op; an out-of-range page number echoes back rather than clamping).
They are documented as the contract and flagged for stakeholder review — not
silently "fixed."

===specs/README===
# Behavioral specs (FFFlow L3)

These Gherkin feature files are the **behavioral contract** for the app — what
it does, in present tense, in domain language. They were extracted from the
existing code by FFFlow's `characterize` step, so they describe current
behavior (characterization), not aspirations.

## Layout

One directory per bounded context (matching the Django apps + shared helpers):

```
docs/specs/
  accounts/    authentication, profiles & following, user model
  articles/    feeds, authoring, article model, markdown
  comments/    commenting, comment model
  helpers/     pagination, integrity-error classification, htmx detection
```

Acceptance specs live at a context root; domain/property specs live under
`<context>/domain/`. `*-properties.feature` files hold universal invariants
(tagged `@property-based`) suited to property-based testing with Hypothesis.

## RIDs (requirement IDs)

Every scenario carries a unique `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}` tag. The CONTEXT
segment matches the first directory under `docs/specs/`. These are the anchor
points for traceability: spec → test → code.

131 scenarios, 131 RIDs.

## Gates (both blocking, part of `just check-all`)

- **`just spec-audit`** — `specdrive audit`: every RID is well-formed, unique,
  and its CONTEXT matches its directory.
- **`just spec-verify`** — full spec→test traceability. Runs both test suites,
  emits a JUnit report from each, injects each test's RID(s), merges the
  reports, and runs `specdrive verify` with `strictTraceability` on.
  **131/131 RIDs covered, 0 uncovered.**

## How a test declares the scenario it covers

`specdrive verify` reads RIDs from the JUnit report as
`<property name="rid" value="RID-...">` inside each `<testcase>`. The Django
runner doesn't emit per-test properties, so the mapping lives in
`docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml` (`"<classname>::<test_method>": [RID-...]`) and
`scripts/inject_rids.py` writes the properties into the report. 15 tests are
deliberately unmapped (`@NOSPEC`) — seed/CLI commands and bare GET-render
smoke tests with no behavioral scenario.

## Two test suites

- **Django suite** (`apps/*/tests.py`, `helpers/tests.py`, `manage.py test`) —
  the 124 example/behavioral tests, including `hypothesis.extra.django`
  property tests for DB-backed invariants (slug stability, email-identity,
  self-follow).
- **Property suite** (`specs/property/`, pytest + `pytest-bdd-property`) — binds
  the DB-free `@property-based` pagination scenarios directly to the Gherkin
  feature file; Hypothesis generates 100+ inputs per scenario.

## `@unverified-intent`

Seven scenarios carry a `# @unverified-intent:` comment. These pin behavior
that is *currently* true but may be an unintended quirk (e.g. a self-follow is a
silent no-op; an out-of-range page number echoes back rather than clamping).
They are documented as the contract and flagged for stakeholder review — not
silently "fixed."

This document lists every CSS class, HTML attribute, text label, route, and
interface that the shared e2e tests depend on. Any RealWorld implementation
that wants to use these tests **must** provide all of the selectors below.

| `.user-pic`     | `img`   | Small avatar in the navbar    |

| Class         | Element   | Purpose                        |
| ------------- | --------- | ------------------------------ |
| `.pagination` | `nav/div` | Pagination container           |
| `.page-item`  | `li/div`  | Individual page button wrapper |

### Buttons

| Class                  | Element  | Purpose                        |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `.btn-outline-primary` | `button` | Favorite (not yet favorited)   |
| `.btn-primary`         | `button` | Unfavorite (already favorited) |
| `.btn-outline-danger`  | `button` | Destructive action (logout)    |

### Errors

| Class             | Element | Purpose                     |
| ----------------- | ------- | --------------------------- |
| `.error-messages` | `ul`    | Validation / API error list |

Buttons and links are located by visible text via `:has-text()`.

| `Update Settings`         | `button` | Settings                 |

from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=()):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)

class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)


class MarkdownFilterTest(TestCase):
    def test_renders_markdown_and_sanitizes(self):

        html = render_markdown("<script>alert(1)</script>ok")
        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)

    def setUp(self):

        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")

        self.art2 = make_article(self.bob, title="Post Two", tags=["django"])

    def test_anonymous_home_shows_all(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "global")

    def test_tag_query_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?tag=python")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "tag")

    def test_tag_url_path_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("tag", args=["django"]))
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")

class ArticleCreateViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()

    def test_anonymous_redirects(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_create"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_get_renders_form(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_create"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_post_creates_article_with_tags(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "New Title", "description": "d", "body": "b", "tags": "python,  django  , "},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        art = Article.objects.get(title="New Title")
        self.assertEqual(art.author, self.alice)
        self.assertEqual(art.summary, "d")
        self.assertEqual(art.content, "b")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(t.name for t in art.tags.all()), ["django", "python"])

    def test_post_creates_article_without_tags(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "No Tags", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(Article.objects.get(title="No Tags").tags.count(), 0)

    def test_post_invalid_form_rerenders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_create"), {"title": "", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_post_redirects_to_new_article_detail(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "Land Here", "description": "d", "body": "b", "tags": ""},
        )
        art = Article.objects.get(title="Land Here")
        self.assertRedirects(resp, reverse("article_detail", args=[art.slug]))


class ArticleEditViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.article = make_article(self.alice, title="Edit Me", tags=["python"])

    def test_non_author_gets_404(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

    def test_get_prefills_form(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Edit Me")
        self.assertContains(resp, "python")

    def test_post_updates_article(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]),
            {"title": "Edit Me", "description": "new desc", "body": "new body", "tags": "rust"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.article.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.article.summary, "new desc")
        self.assertEqual(self.article.content, "new body")
        self.assertEqual([t.name for t in self.article.tags.all()], ["rust"])

    def test_post_invalid_form_rerenders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]),
            {"title": "", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_author_can_delete(self):

        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_delete", args=[self.article.slug]))

class ArticleFavoriteViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.article = make_article(self.alice, title="Fav Me")

    def test_anonymous_redirects(self):
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_toggle_favorite_on_and_off(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertRedirects(resp, reverse("article_detail", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertTrue(self.article.favorites.filter(pk=self.bob.pk).exists())

        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertFalse(self.article.favorites.filter(pk=self.bob.pk).exists())

    def test_htmx_returns_partial(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]), HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_unknown_slug_404(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=["ghost"]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)


class ProfileViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")

    def test_articles_tab_lists_users_own_articles_newest_first(self):

    def test_favorites_tab_lists_favorited_articles_newest_first(self):
        first = make_article(self.bob, title="Fav First")

        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        articles = list(resp.context["articles"])
        self.assertEqual([a.pk for a in articles], [second.pk, first.pk])
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["tab"], "favorites")

    def test_unknown_username_returns_404(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("profile", args=["ghost"]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/working/ffflow-plugin/plugin/skills/plan-chat

# plan-chat

## Plan Mode

This skill does NOT invoke Plan Mode. Claude Code's Plan Mode and FFFlow plans are different things — this skill creates an FFFlow plan on disk by writing files and confirming with the user, not by entering Plan Mode.

## Purpose

Stand up a working plan directory for one change. By the end of the session there is a sealed `<plan-dir>/plan.md` describing the path from current to target spec, plus a `decisions.md` capturing every choice made — with **zero open `?` markers**.

## When to invoke

- A new behavior change is about to start.
- Useful at every level. The artifact format changes with level; the workflow doesn't.

## Inputs

- A description of the change (free-form, from the user).
- `.ffflow/config.yaml` — read for level, stack, capture backend.

## Outputs

Where `<plan-dir>` = `/tmp/ffflow-plans/<project-hash>/<slug>/` (project-hash from `sha256(pwd) | head -c 16`, same convention as `notetoself`).

- `<plan-dir>/plan.md` — the plan itself.
- `<plan-dir>/decisions.md` — every decision made + rejected alternatives. Zero open `?` markers when sealed.
- `<plan-dir>/chat-log.md` — optional running transcript for archaeology.
- `<plan-dir>/metadata.json` — slug, phase, created date, level.
- Optionally a draft spec delta (`<plan-dir>/spec-delta.md`) showing the proposed spec change.

## Dependencies

- Level-appropriate methodology skills, loaded as reference context:
  - L1+: `hexagonal-architecture`, `defect-driven-specification`.
  - L2+: `writing-specs`, `spec-first-development`, `contract-enforcement`.
  - L3: `rid-traceability`, `total-specification`, `quality-gates`.

## Flow

### 0. Setup

1. Read `.ffflow/config.yaml`. If absent, prompt the user to run `/init-ffflow` first and stop.
2. Ask for a short kebab-case slug for the plan (e.g. `auth-token-refresh`).
3. Create `<plan-dir>/`. If one already exists for this slug, offer to resume rather than overwrite.
4. Write a skeleton `plan.md` with the three phase headings and the slug + level recorded at the top.
5. Write `metadata.json` with `phase: chat-incomplete`.

### 1. Understanding

Clarify scope. Ask sharp questions early.

- What problem does this solve? Who benefits?
- What does the current evergreen spec say about this area? Read it before asking the user.
- What exists in the code? Scan for related modules / ports / adapters / spec entries.
- What's out of scope? Mark explicitly.
- What constraints apply? Performance, security, compatibility, deadline.

Do not move on until the user confirms the problem statement. Write the confirmed problem statement into `plan.md` Phase 1.

### 2. Architecture / Approach

Design the path through the code.

- **L0**: prose. "We'll add X to module Y. The contract is: input A → output B." That's enough.
- **L1**: prose + hexagonal layer mapping. Which port? Which adapter? Where does the new code sit?
- **L2**: prose + draft Gherkin Rules + Scenarios. Tag `@property-based` candidates. Identify spec types per layer.
- **L3**: above, plus draft RIDs (`@RID-XXX` placeholders), mutation-testing scope, contract enforcement plan.

Surface decisions as you go. Open ones use `?` markers in `decisions.md`:

```
? Should token refresh happen on every request or only when expiring < 5 min?
```

Write decisions to `decisions.md` continuously as conversation proceeds. Don't batch them at the end.

### 3. Path

Describe the change as a sequence of steps that will become tasks. This is not the same as `plan-breakdown` (which decomposes into independent chess moves), but it does the rough cut.

- Which parts of the spec change, in what order?
- What depends on what?
- Where are the natural commit boundaries?

Write to Phase 3 of `plan.md`.

### 4. Resolve every open decision

**This skill does not seal until every `?` marker in `decisions.md` is resolved.** No exceptions.

For each open `?`:

1. **Restate the question** in plain language. Don't dump the `?` block back; rephrase.
2. **Present 2–3 alternatives**, each with:
   - A concrete name.
   - A one-line tradeoff (cost vs. benefit).
   - Implications for spec, implementation, or downstream work.
   Use evidence where available — file references, similar past decisions, prior plans in `/tmp/ffflow-plans/<project-hash>/`.
3. **Name a recommendation.** Don't be neutral. The user can override; abstaining wastes their time.
4. **Ask for confirmation.** Either "go with X" or "different — tell me which."
5. **Record the answer** in `decisions.md` with rejected alternatives:

   ```
   ✓ Token refresh strategy
      Chose: threshold-based (refresh when < 5min remaining)
      Rationale: balances network overhead against the auth-failure cliff for users on slow networks.
      Rejected alternatives:
        - every request: too much network traffic
        - on 401 retry: too much latency for unhappy paths
   ```

6. If the decision changes content in Phase 2 or Phase 3 of `plan.md`, update those sections — don't strand stale text.

If the user wants to **defer** a decision, write `? (deferred): <reason>` and continue. The skill will still refuse to seal — `plan-breakdown` requires zero opens.

### 5. Seal

Plan is sealed when:

- Zero open `?` markers in `decisions.md` (deferred markers count as open).
- User confirms "ready to break this down."

Update `metadata.json`:
```json
{
  "phase": "chat-complete",
  "ready_for_breakdown": true
}
```

Print:
```
✓ <plan-dir>/ sealed (chat-complete)
Next: /plan-breakdown
```

## Resume

Re-running `plan-chat` against an existing plan directory:
1. Read `metadata.json`. If `phase: chat-complete` and user is starting a new direction, refuse — they should start a new plan slug, or revert the metadata explicitly.
2. Otherwise, read `plan.md` and `decisions.md`. If any `?` markers exist, jump to step 4 (resolve every open decision). Otherwise, pick up at the latest unfinished phase.

## Friction addressed

- Plan Mode misfires (200+ turn chats inside Plan Mode that should have been writing to disk).
- Bloated chats that lose context after `/clear`. Plan files persist.
- Hand-pasted "walk me through alternatives" templates — now part of the chat's discipline.
- Plans that "seal" with open questions, then surprise everyone at breakdown time.
- Specs falling behind — plan optionally writes a spec-delta to commit alongside the work.

## Anti-patterns

- Don't write final RIDs here. Placeholders only — RIDs assigned at capture.
- Don't decompose into tasks here — that's `plan-breakdown`'s job.
- Don't try to do all three phases in one turn. Confirm each phase with the user.
- Don't write code. Plans describe intent.
- Don't seal with open `?`s. The discipline is what makes breakdown clean.
- Don't recommend "it depends" — pick something.
- Don't lose rejected alternatives. Future archaeology needs them.

## Quality checks before sealing

- [ ] Problem statement recorded in `plan.md` Phase 1, confirmed by user.
- [ ] Architecture/approach written in Phase 2, with level-appropriate detail.
- [ ] Path written in Phase 3.
- [ ] `decisions.md` has zero open `?` markers (including deferred).
- [ ] `metadata.json` shows `chat-complete`.
- [ ] At L2+, draft Gherkin parses if any was written.

# Plan: article-drafts

- Slug: `article-drafts`
- Level: L3
- Project: realworld-django-htmx

## Phase 1 — Understanding (problem statement)

Authors currently publish an article the instant they save it — there is no
intermediate "work in progress" state. We want a **draft** capability: an author
can save an article as a draft while still working on it, and publish it when
ready.

Confirmed requirements:

1. Add an `is_published` boolean to the `Article` model. It must default to
   **published** so that every article that exists today (and every article
   created by a code path that doesn't opt in) stays visible — nothing that is
   currently visible disappears.
2. The article editor lets the author choose whether a save publishes the
   article or keeps it as a draft.
3. An author has a way to see their own drafts.

Scope boundaries:

- **In scope:** model field + migration; hiding drafts from public reading
  surfaces (global/following/tag feeds, public profile listings, other users'
  detail views); editor publish-or-draft control; an author-only drafts surface.
- **Out of scope:** scheduled publishing, draft autosave, draft sharing links,
  revision history, per-draft collaborators. (YAGNI — not requested.)

Constraints:

- **Selectors contract** (`realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md`): the `Publish
  Article` button text and the `title`/`description`/`body`/`tags` field names
  are pinned by the e2e suite. The draft control must be *additive* — it must not
  rename or remove the pinned `Publish Article` button, and the existing e2e flow
  (fill fields, click `Publish Article`) must still produce a published article.
- **L3 gates:** every new behavior needs a RID-tagged scenario, a rid_map entry,
  a unit test, and must keep 100% coverage + `spec-audit` + `spec-verify` green.
- **Slug stability / existing invariants** must be preserved.

## Phase 2 — Architecture / Approach

### Model (`apps/articles/models.py`)

Add `is_published = models.BooleanField(default=True, db_index=True)`. Default
`True` satisfies requirement 1 both for the data migration (existing rows) and
for any object created without specifying the flag. `db_index=True` because the
feed querysets filter on it on the hot path.

Migration `0004_article_is_published` — `AddField` with `default=True`; Django
backfills existing rows to `True`.

Draft RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-001` — a new article is published by default.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-002` — an article can be saved unpublished (a draft).

### Reading visibility (feeds + profile listings)

A draft is private to its author. The public listing surfaces must exclude
unpublished articles:

- `_feed_queryset` (global / following / tag) filters `is_published=True`.
- `profile_view` "my articles" and "favorites" tabs filter `is_published=True`
  (a public profile never leaks a user's drafts, even to the author — the author
  has a dedicated drafts surface instead).

Draft RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-FEED-PUBLISHED-001` — feeds show only published articles.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-PUBLISHED-001` — profile listings show only published.

### Article detail visibility (`article_detail_view`)

An unpublished article's detail page is viewable by its author (so they can
preview the draft) but returns 404 to everyone else, so drafts don't leak by URL
guessing. Detail rendering is otherwise `@NOSPEC` today; this adds the first
behavioral scenarios for the detail surface.

Draft RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-001` — the author can view their own draft.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-002` — a non-author gets 404 for a draft.

### Editor control (form + template + create/edit views)

Add a second submit action to the editor: keep the pinned `Publish Article`
button (publishes) and add a `Save Draft` button (saves unpublished). The view
reads the submit intent: a `draft` action ⇒ `is_published=False`, anything else
(including the existing e2e path and every existing unit test that posts without
the field) ⇒ `is_published=True`. This keeps `Publish Article` authoritative and
additive, and preserves all existing tests and the e2e flow unchanged.

`_save_article_form` gains the `is_published` assignment derived from the submit
action. On edit, both buttons are present so an author can publish a draft or
unpublish a published article.

Draft RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-DRAFT-001` — publishing via `Publish Article` creates a
  published article (regression guard for the pinned button).
- `@RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-DRAFT-002` — saving via `Save Draft` creates a draft.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-DRAFT-001` — an author publishes an existing draft.

### Author drafts surface (`?feed=drafts`)

Add a `drafts` feed to `_feed_queryset` — the documented extension point. It
returns the signed-in author's own unpublished articles. An anonymous request
for `?feed=drafts` redirects to login (mirroring the existing `following`
contract). Add a `Your Drafts` tab to the feed toggle, shown only to
authenticated users.

Draft RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-FEED-DRAFTS-001` — an author sees their own drafts in the
  drafts feed.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-FEED-DRAFTS-002` — the drafts feed excludes others' drafts and
  published articles.

intermediate "work in progress" state. We want a **draft** capability: an author
can save an article as a draft while still working on it, and publish it when
ready.

   article or keeps it as a draft.

Scope boundaries:

- **In scope:** model field + migration; hiding drafts from public reading
  surfaces (global/following/tag feeds, public profile listings, other users'

# Plan: article-drafts

- **Slug:** article-drafts
- **Level:** L3 (python, capture: github-issues)
- **Context:** articles

## Phase 1 — Understanding (problem statement)

Authors currently publish an article the instant they save it: every `Article`
is world-visible in feeds and at its detail URL the moment it exists. There is
no way to keep a work-in-progress private.

**Goal:** let an author save an article as a *draft* (not publicly visible) and
*publish* it when ready.

Requirements (from the request):
1. Add an `is_published` boolean to `Article`. Existing articles must remain
   published — default published, so nothing currently visible disappears.
2. The article editor can set whether an article is published or a draft.
3. An author has a way to see their own drafts.

**Beneficiaries:** authors (can iterate privately); readers (feeds stay curated,
no half-finished posts).

**In scope**
- `Article.is_published` field + migration (default `True`).
- Editor publish/draft toggle (create + edit).
- Draft *invisibility*: drafts excluded from global/following/tag feeds, from
  public profile article lists, and from the detail page for anyone but the
  author (otherwise "draft" leaks and the feature is meaningless).
- A **drafts feed** (`/?feed=drafts`) + "Your Drafts" nav pill so the author can
  see their own drafts.

**Out of scope**
- Scheduled/timed publishing, draft autosave, per-draft sharing links.
- Seed-data drafts (would perturb the e2e baseline counts).
- Any change to comment or favorite mechanics beyond the visibility gate they
  inherit for free.

**Constraints**
- `just check-all` stays green: ruff, `ty`, 100% coverage (96% floor),
  `specdrive audit`, `specdrive verify` strict traceability.
- e2e baseline (74 passed / 65 skipped / 0 failed) must not regress. The e2e
  `createArticle` helper never touches a draft control and always clicks
  "Publish Article", so the toggle **must default to published**.
- SELECTORS.md contract: do not rename pinned form fields or button/label text.
  New field `is_published` and new pill text "Your Drafts" are additive and not
  pinned — safe.

## Phase 2 — Architecture / Approach

### Layer mapping (hexagonal)
- **Domain** (`articles/models.py`): the `is_published` field is the new state.
  `ArticleQuerySet` gains a `published()` filter — the single, named place the
  "publicly visible" rule lives, so every reading surface composes the same
  predicate rather than open-coding `filter(is_published=True)`.
- **Application/adapter** (`articles/views.py`, `forms.py`): the editor form
  carries the toggle; `_feed_queryset` gains a `drafts` branch and applies
  `published()` to public feeds; `article_detail_view` and `profile_view` gate
  on visibility.
- **Presentation** (templates): editor checkbox; "Your Drafts" pill.

### Visibility contract (the core rule)
An article is **publicly visible** iff `is_published` is true. Consequences:
- Global / following / tag feeds: published only.
- Public profile article & favorites lists: published only.
- Detail page: published articles are visible to all; a draft is visible only to
  its author (everyone else gets the normal 404).
- Drafts feed (`/?feed=drafts`): the signed-in viewer's own unpublished
  articles; anonymous request redirects to login (mirrors the following feed).

### Draft RIDs (placeholders — final IDs assigned at capture)
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DEFAULT-xxx` — a new article is published by default.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-QUERYSET-xxx` — `published()` returns only published.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-TOGGLE-xxx` — editor publishes when the box is set.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DRAFT-xxx` — editor saves a draft when the box is clear.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-EDIT-xxx` — editing toggles state both ways.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-PREFILL-xxx` — editor reflects the current state.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-FEED-HIDDEN-xxx` — drafts absent from public feeds.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-PROFILE-HIDDEN-xxx` — drafts absent from profile lists.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-xxx` — draft detail: author yes, others 404.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-FEED-OWN-xxx` — drafts feed lists the viewer's own drafts.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-FEED-AUTH-xxx` — anonymous drafts feed → login.

### Mutation-testing scope
The `published()` predicate and the `is_published` assignment in
`_save_article_form` are the highest-value mutants (boolean flip, filter
removal). Every branch is pinned by a dedicated scenario+test below.

### Contract enforcement
No new port/adapter boundary; the visibility rule is enforced at the queryset
(`published()`) so adapters can't drift from it independently.

## Phase 3 — Path (rough cut → chess moves)

1. **Domain: `is_published` field + `published()` queryset** (+ migration).
   Foundation; nothing else compiles a draft without the field.
2. **Editor toggle** — form field, `_save_article_form` wiring, editor template,
   prefill. Depends on 1.
3. **Draft invisibility** — `published()` on public feeds, profile lists gated,
   detail page author-gate. Depends on 1 (and 2 for meaningful drafts to hide).
4. **Drafts feed + nav pill** — `_feed_queryset` `drafts` branch, "Your Drafts"
   pill. Depends on 1–3.

Natural commit boundary per move; each is independently green under
`just check-all`.

# Decisions: article-drafts

All decisions resolved — zero open `?` markers.

✓ **How to represent draft state on the model**
   Chose: a single `is_published = BooleanField(default=True)`.
   Rationale: matches the requirement verbatim; `default=True` makes both the
   data migration and any non-opting-in code path keep articles visible.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - `status` CharField enum (draft/published/…): over-engineered for a
       boolean requirement (YAGNI); no third state is requested.
     - `published_at` nullable datetime: conflates "is it public" with "when",
       and invites scheduled-publishing scope creep.

✓ **Where an author sees their own drafts**
   Chose: a `drafts` feed on the home feed toggle (`?feed=drafts`), mirroring
   the existing `following` feed.
   Rationale: `apps/articles/CLAUDE.md` names `_feed_queryset` as the single
   extraction point for new feed types and lists "drafts" explicitly; the feed
   toggle is the idiomatic RealWorld surface; reuses pagination/HTMX pipeline.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - A drafts tab on the profile page: profiles are public; a drafts tab there
       risks leaking drafts and muddies the "public profile" contract.
     - A standalone `/drafts` page: duplicates the feed pipeline for no benefit.

✓ **Whether the public profile shows the author their own drafts**
   Chose: no — profile listings (both tabs) show only published articles for
   everyone including the owner. Drafts live only on the drafts feed.
   Rationale: keeps one simple rule ("a profile is public, publics see only
   published") and avoids per-viewer branching in the profile queryset.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Show drafts to the owner on their own profile: adds viewer-dependent
       filtering and a second drafts surface; more code, more test matrix.

✓ **Editor publish-vs-draft control**
   Chose: two submit buttons — the pinned `Publish Article` (publishes) plus a
   new `Save Draft` (saves unpublished); the view derives `is_published` from
   the submit action (`draft` ⇒ False, else True).
   Rationale: additive — never renames/removes the pinned `Publish Article`
   button, keeps the e2e flow producing a published article, and preserves every
   existing unit test (which posts without the field ⇒ published). Buttons map
   directly to intent and work symmetrically for publishing a draft or
   unpublishing on edit.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - A "Publish this article" checkbox checked by default: an absent checkbox
       reads as False, so existing dict-posting unit tests would silently become
       drafts; "absent = published" isn't expressible cleanly with a checkbox.
     - A "Save as draft" checkbox: works, but a lone submit button plus a
       contradicting checkbox ("Publish Article" + "save as draft" checked) is a
       confusing control; two explicit buttons read better.

✓ **Draft article detail visibility**
   Chose: the author can view their own draft's detail page; any other viewer
   (including anonymous) gets the existing 404 not-found response.
   Rationale: authors must preview drafts; drafts must not leak by URL. Reuses
   the existing detail 404 path — no new surface.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Drafts fully inaccessible even to the author: breaks preview.
     - Drafts visible to anyone with the link: leaks unpublished content.

✓ **Favorites tab / favoriting and drafts**
   Chose: the profile favorites tab filters to published articles too (same
   published-only rule as the articles tab); no change to the favorite action.
   Rationale: drafts aren't publicly visible so can't be favorited by others in
   normal flow; filtering the favorites listing to published keeps the
   "public profile shows only published" rule uniform with no special-casing.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Leave favorites unfiltered: a self-favorited draft could surface on the
       public favorites tab — an inconsistent leak.

✓ **Index on `is_published`**
   Chose: `db_index=True`.
   Rationale: every feed queryset filters on it on the request hot path.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - No index: simpler migration but a table scan on the busiest query.

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/working/ffflow-plugin/plugin/skills/plan-breakdown

# plan-breakdown

## Plan Mode

This skill does NOT invoke Plan Mode. Task files are written directly.

## Purpose

Take a sealed plan and slice it into 3–8 independently-shippable tasks ("chess moves"). Each task becomes one PR, one branch, one issue.

## When to invoke

- After `plan-chat` has sealed the plan (zero open `?` markers).
- Re-run to refine task boundaries before capture.

## Inputs

- Path to a plan directory (`<plan-dir>/`). If only one in-flight plan exists, default to it.
- `.ffflow/config.yaml` — read for level (changes the task body schema).

## Outputs

- `<plan-dir>/tasks/task-1.md`, `task-2.md`, … one file per chess move.
- `<plan-dir>/metadata.json` updated to `phase: breakdown-complete` with a tasks array.

## Dependencies

None directly. Level-aware reference to methodology skills only.

## Hard gates

**Refuses to run if:**

1. `<plan-dir>/decisions.md` has any **open** `?` markers — tells the user to resume `plan-chat` to resolve them (`plan-chat` doesn't seal until they're all answered).
2. `<plan-dir>/metadata.json` shows `phase: chat-incomplete` — tells the user to finish `plan-chat` first.

These are non-negotiable. Plans get decomposed only after they're sealed.

**What counts as an open marker (avoid false positives).** An *open* marker is a line that starts with `?` or a heading that starts with `## ?`, or any item under a `## Open decisions (?)` section — per the decision-marker convention in `CLAUDE.md`. It is **not** any occurrence of `?` anywhere in the file. Resolved decisions and prose questions do not count:

- A resolved decision must not retain `?` in its heading. Rewrite `## ? D1 — …` to `## D1 — … (resolved)` once answered; don't leave the marker as archival decoration, or this gate trips on history.
- Do not append a "for the record / original options" block that preserves the old `## ?` headings verbatim — strip or de-mark them. The resolution text at the top is the record.
- A `?` inside a sentence (e.g. "should we cache here?") is prose, not a marker. Only line-leading `?` / `## ?` / the Open-decisions section gate the run.

When the gate trips, report *which* lines matched so the user can see whether they're genuinely open or stale markers to clean up.

## Flow

### 1. Load context

- Read `plan.md`, `decisions.md`, `metadata.json`.
- Read any draft spec delta or Gherkin files in the plan dir.
- If the plan references existing spec entries (e.g., "extends `docs/specs/auth.md` Rule 3"), open those too.

### 2. Propose task boundaries

A good chess move is:

- **Freestanding.** Mergeable on its own without breaking main.
- **Bounded.** Explicit out-of-scope list. The next agent doesn't have to guess.
- **Red/green-able.** A test can be written that fails before the code is written, and passes after.
- **One behavior.** Adds or modifies one Rule (L2+) or one prose spec section (L0/L1).

**UI work (stack includes `typescript-ui`): decompose component-first.** Per `component-driven-ui`, a feature with a UI splits so the presentational components come *before* the container that wires them. Earlier tasks build and prove atoms/molecules/organisms (component + story + test); a later task integrates the proven components into the app. A task that wires an unbuilt component into app code is mis-scoped — split the component out. The "no app import before proven" ordering becomes a task dependency: the integration task `depends on` the component tasks.

Propose 3–8 tasks. Present them to the user as a short list:

```
Proposed tasks:
  1. Add password complexity Rule + validator port (no UI changes)
  2. Wire password validator into signup adapter
  3. Add token-refresh threshold logic (depends on 1)
  4. Update CLI auth flow to use new validator (depends on 2)

Looks right? Anything to split, merge, or reorder?
```

Iterate with the user until they confirm.

### 3. Write task files

One file per chess move. Body shape varies by level:

#### L0 (prose)

```markdown
# Task 1: Add password complexity validator

## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/auth.md` §"Password complexity" (new section to be written).

The system rejects passwords that are < 8 chars or contain no digit.

## Implementation scope
- New module: `src/auth/password_validator.py`
- Modified: `src/auth/signup.py` — call validator before persisting.
- Test: `tests/auth/test_password_validator.py`.

## Out of scope
- UI error messaging changes (see task 4)
- Existing password migration

## Acceptance
- [ ] Validator rejects passwords matching the rules above.
- [ ] Signup integration uses the validator.
- [ ] All existing auth tests still pass.
- [ ] Spec section written and committed in the same PR.

## Depends on
None.
```

#### L1 (prose + layer mapping)

Adds:
```markdown
## Hexagonal layer
- Domain: `PasswordPolicy` value object (pure)
- Application: `PasswordValidatorPort` interface
- Infrastructure: `RegexPasswordValidator` adapter
```

#### L2 (Gherkin scope)

```markdown
## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/auth.feature` Rule "Password complexity".
Scenarios: 3 new (covering happy path, too-short, no-digit).

## Step definitions
New: `Given a user submitting password <pw>`, `Then signup is <result>`.
```

#### L3 (full Gherkin + RIDs + property tests)

```markdown
## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/auth.feature` Rule "Password complexity".
RIDs: @RID-PWD-001 through @RID-PWD-003.
Property tests: @property-based scenario covering random strings against the policy.

## Mutation testing
This module must reach 80% mutation score before merge.
```

Each task ends with:
- `## Out of scope` — explicit boundary.
- `## Acceptance` — checklist.
- `## Depends on` — other tasks by id, or "None."

### 4. Interactive review

For each task, ask:
- Is this freestanding? (Could it merge alone?)
- Is the out-of-scope list honest? (No scope creep?)
- Is the test writable before the code? (If no, rewrite the task.)

Iterate. Don't move on until the user signs off.

### 5. Update metadata and report

`metadata.json`:
```json
{
  "phase": "breakdown-complete",
  "tasks": [
    {"id": "task-1", "title": "...", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "task-2", "title": "...", "depends_on": ["task-1"]}
  ]
}
```

Report:
```
✓ <plan-dir>/ → 4 tasks
Next: /plan-capture
```

## Resume

Re-running:
- If `phase: breakdown-complete` and user wants to refine, allow edits to existing task files in place. Don't duplicate.
- If new tasks appear, append them with the next index.

## Friction addressed

- Plan-then-breakdown loops where breakdown reveals new design questions (caught by the `?` hard gate).
- Tasks that look done but leave PR authors archaeologizing the original plan (each task is self-contained).
- Scope creep mid-PR (explicit out-of-scope list).

## Anti-patterns

- Don't write infrastructure-only tasks ("set up CI") — those go in `stack-init`.
- Don't write test-only tasks at L2+ — tests travel with the implementation. Exception: characterize backfill tasks, which are intentionally tests-only.
- Don't propose 12 tiny tasks. Anything more than 8 means the plan was too big.
- Don't strand the spec change. Each task's PR carries its spec delta.

## Quality checks before sealing

- [ ] 3–8 tasks.
- [ ] Each task maps to specific spec content (sections, Rules, or RIDs).
- [ ] No spec content left unassigned.
- [ ] Each task is freestanding or has explicit `depends_on`.
- [ ] `out_of_scope` field non-empty for every task.
- [ ] `metadata.json` shows `breakdown-complete`.


ARGUMENTS: article-drafts
Gate check: no open `?` markers in decisions.md. Writing the 5 task files.

# Task 2: Editor — publish/draft toggle

## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/articles/authoring.feature` — new Rule
"An author chooses whether to publish or save a draft".
RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-TOGGLE-001` — submitting with the publish box set
  creates a published article.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DRAFT-001` — submitting with the publish box clear
  saves the article as a draft.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-EDIT-001` — editing an article flips its state both ways.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-PREFILL-001` — the editor reflects the article's current
  publication state when opened.

## Hexagonal layer
- Application/adapter: `ArticleForm.is_published` (`BooleanField(required=False)`);
  `_save_article_form` writes `article.is_published`.
- Presentation: `templates/articles/editor.html` checkbox `name="is_published"`.

## Implementation scope
- `apps/articles/forms.py` — add `is_published` BooleanField (required=False,
  checkbox widget). Do NOT rename `title`/`description`/`body`/`tags`.
- `apps/articles/views.py` — `_save_article_form` sets `is_published` from
  cleaned data; edit view prefill includes current state; create view renders
  the box checked by default.
- `templates/articles/editor.html` — checkbox + label above "Publish Article".
  Keep the pinned button text.
- `apps/articles/tests.py` — create-published, create-draft, edit-toggle,
  prefill cases. Update existing create/edit tests that assert published
  behavior to set the box.
- `docs/specs/rid_map.articles.yaml` — map the new tests.

## Out of scope
- Making drafts invisible anywhere (task 3) — a draft created here is still
  publicly visible until task 3 lands. That's an acceptable intermediate state.
- The drafts feed (task 4).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Editor renders a checkbox defaulting to checked for a new article.
- [ ] POST with box set → `is_published=True`; box clear → `False`.
- [ ] Edit prefills and toggles state both directions.
- [ ] Button text "Publish Article" unchanged (SELECTORS contract).
- [ ] `just check-all` green (100% coverage held); e2e create flow unaffected.

## Depends on
task-1.

# Task 4: Editor can publish or save as draft

## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/articles/authoring.feature` — new Rule "The editor saves as a
draft or publishes, and the author can change that on edit".
RIDs:
- @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-DRAFT-001 — clicking `Publish Article` creates a published
  article (regression guard for the pinned button + existing e2e flow).
- @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-DRAFT-002 — clicking `Save Draft` creates a draft.
- @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-DRAFT-001 — an author publishes an existing draft from the editor.

## Implementation scope
- `apps/articles/views.py`:
  - `_save_article_form(form, article, publish)` — set `article.is_published`
    from a `publish` boolean derived by the caller.
  - `article_create_view` / `article_edit_view` — derive publish intent from the
    submit action: `is_published = request.POST.get("action") != "draft"` (any
    value other than `draft`, including a missing action, ⇒ publish). Pass it into
    `_save_article_form`.
- `templates/articles/editor.html` — keep the pinned `Publish Article` submit
  button (add `name="action" value="publish"`) and add a second submit button
  `name="action" value="draft"` labelled `Save Draft`.
- `apps/articles/tests.py` — create-published (action=publish), create-draft
  (action=draft), edit publishes a draft (action=publish on a draft).
- `docs/specs/rid_map.articles.yaml` — map new tests to the new RIDs.
- Update `apps/articles/CLAUDE.md` (`_save_article_form` bullet) for the new
  `publish` argument.

## Out of scope
- The drafts feed / how the author browses drafts (task 5).
- Do NOT rename or remove the `Publish Article` button text, nor the
  `title`/`description`/`body`/`tags` field names (SELECTORS.md contract).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `Publish Article` submit ⇒ published article (e2e flow preserved).
- [ ] `Save Draft` submit ⇒ unpublished article.
- [ ] Editing a draft and clicking `Publish Article` publishes it.
- [ ] Existing create/edit unit tests (which post without `action`) still pass
      and still produce published articles.
- [ ] rid_map updated; `spec-audit` + `spec-verify` green.
- [ ] `just check-all` green (100% coverage).

## Depends on
- task-1 (needs the `is_published` field).

# Task 4: Drafts feed + "Your Drafts" nav pill

## Behavioral scope
Spec: `docs/specs/articles/feeds.feature` — new Rule "An author can browse their
own drafts feed".
RIDs:
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-FEED-OWN-001` — the drafts feed lists the signed-in
  viewer's own unpublished articles and excludes published ones and other
  authors' drafts.
- `@RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-FEED-AUTH-001` — an anonymous request for the drafts feed
  is redirected to sign in.

## Hexagonal layer
- Application/adapter: `_feed_queryset` gains a `drafts` branch (author's own
  `is_published=False`; `None` for anonymous → caller redirects to login), active
  tab `"drafts"`.
- Presentation: `templates/partials/feed_content.html` — "Your Drafts" pill for
  authenticated users.

## Implementation scope
- `apps/articles/views.py` — `_feed_queryset` `feed == "drafts"` branch, returns
  `(None, "drafts")` for anonymous, else the viewer's own drafts.
- `templates/partials/feed_content.html` — add the "Your Drafts" nav-link
  (authenticated only) pointing at `/?feed=drafts`, active when
  `active_tab == 'drafts'`.
- `apps/articles/tests.py` — drafts-feed-lists-own, drafts-feed-anonymous-redirect.
- `docs/specs/rid_map.articles.yaml` — map the new tests.

## Out of scope
- Editing/publishing from the drafts feed (the existing editor already covers it).
- Any seed-data drafts.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `/?feed=drafts` (authenticated) → the viewer's own drafts only, newest
      first, active tab "drafts".
- [ ] `/?feed=drafts` (anonymous) → redirect to login.
- [ ] "Your Drafts" pill shows for authenticated users; text does not collide
      with "Your Feed"/"Global Feed" e2e matchers.
- [ ] `just check-all` green (100% coverage held); e2e baseline unaffected.

## Depends on
task-1, task-2, task-3.

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/working/ffflow-plugin/plugin/skills/work-issue

# work-issue

## Plan Mode

This skill does NOT invoke Plan Mode. It executes a single chess move; planning is already done.

## Purpose

Take one captured issue (or task file) from cold-start to a PR. The spec change ships in the same PR as the implementation. At every level, the discipline is the same — only the artifacts scale.

## Inputs

- An issue ID (`/work 42`) or path to a task file (markdown backend).
- `.ffflow/config.yaml` — read for level, stack, capture backend.

## Outputs

- A branch named per the task's `Branch:` field (typically `task/<plan-slug>/task-N-<short-title>`).
- A PR (draft or ready, depending on local-validation results).
- Spec updates committed in the same PR.
- Updated `.ffflow/audit.yaml` if any audited file is touched.

## Dependencies

- `tdd-loop` — the red/green/refactor discipline.
- `self-review` — pre-PR checklist.
- Level-appropriate stack and methodology skills.

## Cross-cutting invariants

These are non-negotiable.

### PR-checkpoint protocol

When ≥ 2 PRs have been created in the current session, pause with a summary:

```
PRs created this session:
  #101 — task-1: ...  (status: open, draft=false, checks=pending)
  #102 — task-2: ...  (status: open, draft=false, checks=pending)

continue? (y/n/disable)
```

- `y` continues; counter resets.
- `n` stops the session.
- `disable` turns off PR-checkpointing for the rest of the session. One decision; no further nags.

The default is the every-2-PRs cadence. `disable` is for users who want to let a long fanout run uninterrupted after they've confirmed it's healthy. Counter and disable-state are session-local — they reset on next invocation.

### Local-validation gate

Before pushing a PR that contains anything other than spec-only changes:

- Either run the project's local repro/smoke (`just test`, `pytest`, `npm test`, level-appropriate) and confirm green, **or**
- State explicitly in the PR body why local validation wasn't possible (e.g., "requires external API access").

A non-spec-only PR with neither is a protocol violation.

## Flow

### Phase 0 — Load and detect state

1. Read `.ffflow/config.yaml` for level/stack.
2. Load the task:
   - Issue ID → `gh issue view <id>` for body and metadata.
   - Task file → read directly.
3. Detect resume state by branch + PR:
   - **Branch exists, PR merged** → done. Exit.
   - **Branch exists, PR open** → resume at Phase 5.
   - **Branch exists, no PR** → resume from where commits left off.
   - **No branch** → create from main: `git checkout -b <branch>`.
4. Verify dependencies are complete (closed PRs / merged branches). If a dep is open, ask the user how to proceed.

### Phase 1 — Read the spec

The task body cites a spec back-link. Open it:

- **L0/L1**: prose spec section. Read the surrounding context.
- **L2**: `.feature` Rule. Read the scenarios in scope.
- **L3**: RID list. Read those scenarios and their bound step definitions.

Re-read the task body once more after reading the spec. Confirm the chess move is still well-defined; if you have new questions, stop and ask the user.

### Phase 2 — TDD loop (delegated to `tdd-loop`)

Load `tdd-loop` as reference context. Walk the loop:

1. Write the test(s) that pin the new behavior. At L2+, this includes any new `.feature` content or scenarios.
2. Run them. They must fail (red). If they pass, the test is wrong or the behavior already exists.
3. Write the minimum code to make them pass.
4. Refactor under green.
5. Repeat per chunk.

Stack-specific commands come from the `stack` skill's cartridge matching `.ffflow/config.yaml stack:`.

**UI work (stack includes `typescript-ui`): the loop is component-first.** Load `component-driven-ui` as reference context. The ordering is a discipline, and at L2+ a gate: decompose the change into components → build each presentational component in isolation → write its story (a vignette per reasonable state) and component test as the "red" → green → assemble upward → **only then** write the container that wires it into the app. Do not import a component into app/container code until its story and test are green (the `ui` audit cartridge enforces this in Phase 4). The story's `play()` interaction test and the component unit test are the tests you write in step 1.

### Phase 3 — Spec update

Update the evergreen spec to reflect the new behavior. This commit goes in the same PR as the implementation.

- L0/L1: edit prose. Cross-reference the task issue in the spec section's footer.
- L2: update or add Rule / Scenarios in the `.feature` file.
- L3: write RID-tagged scenarios; ensure RID uniqueness via `/audit --type rid` (deferred until Phase 4).

### Phase 4 — Gates

Run level-appropriate gates:

- **L0**: lint, format, tests.
- **L1**: above + `/audit --type claude-md` (if any docs changed).
- **L2**: above + `/audit --type spec` for files in scope + `/audit --type char-tests` if any characterization tests are pinned to this spec. **UI stacks:** + `/audit --type ui` (story presence, dependency rule, token conformance, no-unproven-app-import) + `just test-stories`.
- **L3**: full quality gates per `quality-gates`: structure / correctness / coverage / maintainability, including mutation testing for the touched scope. **UI stacks:** `/audit --type ui` blocking at full strictness (story-coverage threshold, token conformance) + optional visual regression.

If any gate fails after honest attempts, mark the PR as draft and surface the failures in the PR body.

### Phase 5 — Self-review

Invoke `self-review` skill. Walk its checklist against this PR's diff. In particular: every minor issue you noticed during implementation should be either **fixed in this PR** (`zero-tech-debt`'s 15-minute rule) or **deferred with a concrete TODO-with-trigger** (`yagni`). No bare TODOs, no vague triggers, no "future work" sections in the PR body.

### Phase 6 — PR

Honor the local-validation gate (above). Then:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "<short title>" \
  --body "<body>"
```

PR body shape:

```markdown
Closes #<issue-id>

## Spec changes
- <file>: <one-line description>

## Implementation
- <file>: <one-line description>

## Tests
- <file>: <added / modified>
- Local result: <pass | fail | not-run + reason>

## Audit
- <auditor>: <pass | fail | n/a>
```

If draft (gates failing): prefix title with `[WIP]` and add `## Outstanding` section listing the open work.

After creating the PR, **post a one-line summary in the session** per the PR-checkpoint protocol:

```
created PR #<n> — task-<id>: <title> (draft=<bool>)
```

## Idempotency

- Re-running on a branch with an open PR resumes at the PR step — checks state, refreshes body if spec/test summary changed, no-ops if already current.
- Commits are atomic per chunk. Mid-loop interruptions resume cleanly because the previous chunk is already on the branch.

## Friction addressed

- PR-author archaeology after long autonomous runs (PR body cites issue, spec, tests).
- Specs falling behind code (single-PR spec+code).
- PRs shipped without local repro (local-validation gate).
- Plan Mode misfires inside execution flows.
- Runaway autonomous loops (PR-checkpoint protocol).

## Anti-patterns

- Don't push a PR without spec changes if the task said the spec should change.
- Don't move past Phase 2 if tests aren't actually red first — that means the test is wrong.
- Don't merge yourself. The human merges (or `autopilot` does, with explicit authorization).
- Don't refactor outside the scope of the task. Refactor opportunities → file a `refactor`-driven plan, not in this PR.
- Don't change spec sections outside the task's scope. If you notice drift, file an audit finding.

## Edge cases

- **Spec back-link missing from task body**: capture wasn't clean. Stop and ask the user — fix the issue, don't proceed.
- **Tests already pass at Phase 2 red step**: behavior already exists somewhere. Investigate. Either the task is a no-op (delete the issue), or there's a duplication problem.
- **Gates fail repeatedly with the same error**: stop, surface to user. Do not self-loop indefinitely.

## Quality checks before PR

- [ ] Task issue read; spec back-link followed.
- [ ] Tests written, ran red, then green.
- [ ] Spec updated in the same branch.
- [ ] Local-validation gate honored (either passed or explained).
- [ ] Level-appropriate audits ran.
- [ ] `self-review` clean.
- [ ] PR body cites issue, spec changes, tests.

from typing import Self

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractBaseUser, AnonymousUser
from django.db import models
from django.utils.text import slugify
from taggit.managers import TaggableManager


class ArticleQuerySet(models.QuerySet):
    def with_favorites(self, user: AbstractBaseUser | AnonymousUser) -> Self:
        return self.annotate(
            num_favorites=models.Count("favorites"),
            is_favorite=(
                models.Exists(get_user_model().objects.filter(pk=user.pk, favorites=models.OuterRef("pk")))
                if user.is_authenticated
                else models.Value(False, output_field=models.BooleanField())
            ),
        )


ArticleManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(ArticleQuerySet)


class Article(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True, blank=False)
    summary = models.TextField(blank=True)
    content = models.TextField(blank=True)

    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    tags = TaggableManager(blank=True)
    favorites = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="favorites")
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True, max_length=255)  # Not a property as used for lookup

    objects = ArticleManager()

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        if not self.pk:
            self.slug = slugify(self.title)
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=()):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)
