# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`).
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets.
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(
        author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published
    )
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Default Published", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)

    def test_article_can_be_created_as_draft(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="A Draft", summary="s", content="c", is_published=False)
        self.assertFalse(a.is_published)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)

        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_toggle_favorite_on_and_off(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertRedirects(resp, reverse("article_detail", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertTrue(self.article.favorites.filter(pk=self.bob.pk).exists())

        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertFalse(self.article.favorites.filter(pk=self.bob.pk).exists())

    def test_htmx_returns_partial(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=[self.article.slug]), HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_unknown_slug_404(self):

        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_favorite", args=["ghost"]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

Feature: Authoring and favoriting articles
  As an author
  I want to create, edit, and delete my own articles, and favorite others' work
  So that I can publish my writing and signal which articles I value

  Authoring is restricted to the article's own author. Favoriting is open to
  any signed-in reader and toggles on each action. Both demand authentication;
  an anonymous visitor is always sent to sign in first.

  Rule: Only a signed-in user may reach the article editor

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor is redirected away from the new-article editor
      When an anonymous visitor opens the new-article editor
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-002
    Scenario: A signed-in author opens the new-article editor
      Given a signed-in author
      When they open the new-article editor
      Then the article editor is presented

  Rule: Publishing an article records its title, summary, body, tags, and author

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-001
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article titled "New Title" with a summary, a body, and the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article is created with that author
      And its summary and body are recorded as entered
      And it carries the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-002
    Scenario: Tag entries are trimmed and blank entries discarded
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article carries exactly the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-003
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with no tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with an empty tag list
      Then the article is created with no tags

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-004
    Scenario: After publishing, the author lands on the new article

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Default Published", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)

    def test_article_can_be_created_as_draft(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="A Draft", summary="s", content="c", is_published=False)
        self.assertFalse(a.is_published)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)

Feature: Authoring and favoriting articles
  As an author
  I want to create, edit, and delete my own articles, and favorite others' work
  So that I can publish my writing and signal which articles I value

  Authoring is restricted to the article's own author. Favoriting is open to
  any signed-in reader and toggles on each action. Both demand authentication;
  an anonymous visitor is always sent to sign in first.

  Rule: Only a signed-in user may reach the article editor

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor is redirected away from the new-article editor
      When an anonymous visitor opens the new-article editor
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-002
    Scenario: A signed-in author opens the new-article editor
      Given a signed-in author
      When they open the new-article editor
      Then the article editor is presented

  Rule: Publishing an article records its title, summary, body, tags, and author

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-001
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article titled "New Title" with a summary, a body, and the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article is created with that author
      And its summary and body are recorded as entered
      And it carries the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-002
    Scenario: Tag entries are trimmed and blank entries discarded
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article carries exactly the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-003
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with no tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with an empty tag list
      Then the article is created with no tags

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-004
    Scenario: After publishing, the author lands on the new article
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish a valid article
      Then they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-005
    Scenario: An article cannot be published without a title
      Given a signed-in author
      When they submit the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may edit their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot edit the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to open the edit editor for that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-002
    Scenario: The author's editor is pre-filled with the current article
      Given a signed-in author with an article titled "Edit Me" tagged "python"
      When they open the edit editor for that article
      Then the editor is pre-filled with "Edit Me"
      And the editor is pre-filled with the tag "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-003
    Scenario: An author edits the summary, body, and tags of their article
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with a new summary, a new body, and the tags "rust"
      Then the article's summary and body are updated
      And the article carries exactly the tag "rust"
      And they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-004
    Scenario: A saved edit cannot leave the title empty
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may delete their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot delete the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to delete that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-002
    Scenario: An author deletes their own article
      Given a signed-in author with an article
      When they delete that article
      Then the article no longer exists
      And they are returned to the home feed

  Rule: A draft's detail page is visible only to its author

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-001
    Scenario: An author can view their own draft
      Given a signed-in author with a draft article
      When they open that draft's detail page
      Then the draft is shown

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-002
    Scenario: A signed-in reader who is not the author cannot view a draft
      Given an author's draft article
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader opens that draft's detail page
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-002
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot view a draft
      Given an author's draft article
      When an anonymous visitor opens that draft's detail page
      Then the article is reported as not found

  Rule: Favoriting requires sign-in and toggles on each action

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot favorite an article
      When an anonymous visitor tries to favorite an article
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-002
    Scenario: Favoriting then favoriting again removes the favorite
      Given a signed-in reader and an article they have not favorited

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Default Published", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)

    def test_article_can_be_created_as_draft(self):

        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="A Draft", summary="s", content="c", is_published=False)
        self.assertFalse(a.is_published)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()

        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)

class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)

class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)

# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` (BooleanField, `default=True`, indexed) marks published vs. draft — default published so existing/unspecified articles stay visible; drafts are hidden from every public reading surface and visible only to their author.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets.
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).

Feature: Browsing article feeds
  As a reader
  I want to browse articles through the global feed, my personalised feed, and tag filters
  So that I can discover the writing that matters to me

  The feed is the home surface for articles. A reader can switch between the
  global feed (every article), their personal "following" feed (articles by
  authors they follow), and a tag-filtered view. All three share one feed
  rendering pipeline: the same composition, the same pagination, and the same
  choice between a full page and an in-place fragment refresh.

  Background:
    Given several published articles exist by various authors

  Rule: The global feed shows every article, newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-001
    Scenario: An anonymous reader sees all articles in the global feed
      Given an article "Post One" and an article "Post Two" exist
      When an anonymous reader opens the home feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the global feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-002
    Scenario: Articles are ordered newest first
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then articles appear in order of most recently created first

  Rule: Feeds never show unpublished draft articles

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-PUBLISHED-001
    Scenario: A draft is absent from the global feed
      Given a published article "Published Post" exists
      And an unpublished draft "Draft Post" exists
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then they see "Published Post"
      And they do not see "Draft Post"

  Rule: The following feed shows only articles by authors the reader follows

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-001
    Scenario: A signed-in reader sees only followed authors' articles
      Given a reader who follows the author of "Post One"
      And the author of "Post Two" is not followed by that reader
      When the reader opens their following feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they do not see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the following feed

    # @unverified-intent: anonymous access to the following feed is handled by a
    # server-side redirect to login rather than hiding the tab; documenting the
    # current contract.
    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-002
    Scenario: An anonymous reader requesting the following feed is sent to sign in
      When an anonymous reader requests the following feed
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

  Rule: A tag filter narrows the feed to articles carrying that tag

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-001
    Scenario: Filtering the feed by a tag query
      Given "Post One" is tagged "python"
      And "Post Two" is tagged "django"
      When a reader filters the home feed by the tag "python"
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they do not see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the tag feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-002
    Scenario: Visiting a tag's own page narrows the feed the same way
      Given "Post Two" is tagged "django"
      When a reader opens the page for the tag "django"
      Then they see "Post Two"
      And they do not see "Post One"

  Rule: The sidebar offers the set of all tags, refreshed on a short cycle

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-003
    Scenario: The feed presents the available tags
      Given articles tagged "python" and "django" exist
      When a reader opens the home feed
      Then the available tags are offered alongside the feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-TAG-004
    Scenario: Newly used tags become available after an article is saved
      Given the available tags have been listed and cached
      When an author publishes an article carrying a brand-new tag
      Then the new tag becomes available to readers immediately

  Rule: Feeds are paginated ten articles to a page

    @RID-ARTICLES-PAGINATION-001
    Scenario: The feed shows at most ten articles per page
      Given more than ten articles exist
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then at most ten articles are shown on the page

    @RID-ARTICLES-PAGINATION-002
    Scenario Outline: A malformed or out-of-bounds page request falls back to the first page
      When a reader opens the feed with a page request of "<requested>"
      Then the feed responds successfully
      And the reader is shown page 1

      Examples:
        | requested |
        | bogus     |
        | 0         |
        | -5        |
        |           |

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Default Published", summary="s", content="c")

    def test_article_can_be_created_as_draft(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="A Draft", summary="s", content="c", is_published=False)
        self.assertFalse(a.is_published)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()

        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)

# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` (BooleanField, `default=True`, indexed) marks published vs. draft — default published so existing/unspecified articles stay visible; drafts are hidden from every public reading surface and visible only to their author.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article, publish)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`) and sets `is_published` from the `publish` flag. **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract. The editor derives `publish` from the submit button: `Save Draft` posts `action=draft` (⇒ draft), the pinned `Publish Article` posts `action=publish`, and any request without `action` defaults to published.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets.
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).
